title: Rabbi Chanina bar Ami

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Bereshit Rabbah 16:3, speaking in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin, who speaks in the name of Rabbi Levi.

notes.text: The abbreviation ב״מ and locator פ״טז־נ remain unresolved. Bamidbar Rabbah was the earlier draft’s proposed expansion, but no matching named-source evidence is supplied for this citation. The transmission chain is retained without claiming absence from a whole work or edition.

Further comparison: Midrash Rabbah -- TE, Bereshit Rabbah 16:3, contains רבי חנינא בר אמי בשם רבי יהושע דסכנין בשם רבי לוי. This locates the exact chain under Bereshit Rabbah, rather than the earlier proposed Bamidbar Rabbah. It does not by itself establish the origin or intended expansion of supplied ב״מ פ״טז־נ, so that locator is preserved.

Hyman’s printed page (vol. II, p. 479) reads ב״ר פ״טז־ג, Bereshit Rabbah 16:3, where the cited chain concerns which river is foremost. Theodor’s edition (p. 144) gives a different patronymic in its main text and records “bar Ami” as a variant.
